title: Nations and States
objective: After this level you can explain the difference between a nation and a state.
summary: A nation is a people with a shared identity; a state has territory, laws and a monopoly of legitimate force. The Kurds are a nation without a state; the UK is one state of four parts.

cards.headline: Tens of millions of Kurds share a nation. They have no state of their own.
cards.body: Britannica estimated the Kurds at 36 to 46 million in the mid-2010s, living mostly in parts of Iran, Iraq, Syria and Turkey. In the modern era they have had no nation-state of their own. How can so many people share a nation but not a state? Because those are two different things.

cards.headline: Nation, state, nation-state
cards.body: A nation is a community of people who share an identity: often a culture, a language or a history. A state is a political organization with territory, laws and the means to enforce them. Put the two together and you get a nation-state. A nation lives in a sense of "us". A state lives in borders, courts and passports.

cards.headline: Weber's test for a state
cards.body: Remember Max Weber from Level 3? In 1919 he defined the state as a human community that successfully claims the monopoly of the legitimate use of physical force within a territory. Only the state gets to use force, through police and courts, and people accept that it's allowed to. It's Level 3's authority, stretched across a whole country.

cards.fact: Nations and states rarely line up neatly.
cards.context: In Britannica's words, the borders of states and the boundaries of nations usually only partly overlap. The Kurds are one nation across several states. It works the other way too: the United Kingdom is one state made of four historical parts, England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, each with its own customs and traditions.

cards.headline: Nation vs state: mapped
learned: A nation: a people with a shared identity
A state: territory, laws and enforcement
Weber: the state monopolizes legitimate force
The Kurds and the UK show they rarely match

questions.prompt: Which best describes the difference between a nation and a state?

options.label: A nation is simply a state with more people in it
options.rationale: Size isn't the difference; identity versus organization is.

options.label: Nation: shared identity. State: territory and laws
A nation has laws and courts; a state never does
options.rationale: It's the other way round: the state is the political organization.

options.label: They are two different words for the same thing
options.rationale: They're different, which is why they don't always line up.

questions.explanation: A nation is a community with a shared identity; a state is a political organization with territory, laws and enforcement.

questions.prompt: Why are the Kurds described as a nation without a state?

options.label: They share an identity but have no state of their own
They have no shared language, culture or history
options.rationale: They're a nation precisely because they share an identity.

options.label: They all live together inside one single country
options.rationale: They live across parts of Iran, Iraq, Syria and Turkey.

options.label: They have chosen to live without any government
options.rationale: They live under the governments of the states they're in.

questions.explanation: The Kurds share an identity as a nation but have had no nation-state of their own in the modern era.

questions.prompt: Weber said a state claims the monopoly of the legitimate use of force. Which Level 3 idea does "legitimate" point to?

options.label: Charisma: a leader's exceptional qualities
options.rationale: Charisma is one root of authority, but legitimacy is about acceptance.

options.label: Free riding on public goods
options.rationale: Free riding is Level 5's problem, not legitimacy.

options.label: The general will
options.rationale: The general will is Rousseau's idea.

questions.explanation: Legitimate force is force people accept: Level 3's authority, stretched across a whole territory.
